answer: An identity must show a public code-review history: reviews left on other people's pull requests, visible in the open, over years. A glacier moves slowly and leaves a deep mark, and a reviewer with hundreds of thoughtful comments does the same. The quartz of a farm's accounts is cloudy: their review history is empty, or all their reviews were posted in one week on each other's repos. A yarrow plant grows a little each season, and so does a real reviewer's record: it cannot be faked in bulk, because every review is public, timestamped, and tied to real code.
